newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Bell says Savage a buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Bell says Savage a buy.

text.p: Bell Securities Ltd has issued a buy recommendation on Savage Resources Ltd, citing a strong growth phase which should position the zinc and coal miner to benefit from the next commodities boom.
Upside would come from the start-up of the Ernest Henry copper mine in Queensland the Glendall coal mine in NSW in 1997, along with a steadily improving zinc market, Bell said in a research report.
Savage also had probable exploration success in gold and base metals and a strong balance sheet.
"Management has delivered well over the past two years and Savage deserves a strong rating in the Australian Base Metal Sector," the report said.

Bell said at sustainable commodity prices of US$0.58 a pound for zinc, US$0.95 a pound for copper and the Australian dollar at US75 cents, Savage should produce sustainable earnings of A$71 million in 1998/99.
Savage has 49 percent of Ernest Henry and 67.5 percent of the Glendall mine.
Its low-cost Tennessee zinc assets, bought in 1994, produced germanium as a valuable by-product, Bell said.
"Although zinc output will remain relatively flat over the next few years, continuous improvements to the mines and refinery will put Savage in a very strong position at higher zinc prices."
Savage was pursuing new zinc reserves in the U.S., Canada and Peru and exploring for gold in Peru and Western Australia.
Shares in Savage were two cents lower at A$1.31 at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), having risen steadily from around A$0.75 over the past eight months.
